records.c: Current slot of the six-entry VIC raster schedule. The hardware interrupt loads the next line before dispatching the selected slot.
Low byte of the three-byte current player's packed decimal score at $19-$1B.
Packed decimal round count. It advances independently of the round-data selector and is saved per player.
Round-data selector in the range 1 through 16 after initialization. The transition routine wraps this selector without wrapping the displayed round at 16.
Horizontal speed tier used by the ground and air movement paths. Fresh directional input can add a tier up to 2.
Signed horizontal input produced by the play control sampler, with $FF for left, 0 for neutral and 1 for right when a single direction is active.
Active-low jump sample after the sampler's edge and hold logic.
Previous release state used by the control sampler to distinguish the first press from a held button.
Horizontal fine-scroll phase. The playfield raster merges it into $D016 and the scrolling routine wraps it to three bits at character boundaries.
Amount added to or subtracted from the fine-scroll phase, depending on the sign of $39.
Its sign selects the left or right column update path in the scroll routine.
Zero means the motion routine uses ground movement. Nonzero selects the airborne path and its sign participates in the air-state checks.
Signed value set by the jump initializer and consulted by the airborne animation and movement code.
Main Pac sprite's vertical VIC position. The terrain routine compares it with the current floor and the interrupt writes it to $D00F.
Pattern number copied to $C7FF to select the main Pac frame for VIC sprite 7.
Player number used to index the paired score, round, lives and restart fields. The handover code selects between indexes 1 and 2.
Packed decimal credits adjusted with decimal arithmetic and displayed at $C7C7/$C7C8.

Initialize the stack and install the reset and NMI signature at $8000. A six-byte match at $0220 takes the erasure path at $0B6E. Otherwise select RAM with I/O visible via $01, initialize hardware and enter the title at $064C.
Reset SID and gameplay workspace, set up video and low stack-page tables, then install and enable the game's raster IRQ and NMI vectors.
Nine bytes copied to $8000 on entry. They hold the reset and NMI words followed by the cartridge signature with final byte $30.
Six signature bytes compared with $0220-$0225 by the startup check.

Save the interrupted registers and clear decimal mode. Advance the raster slot $0E modulo six, schedule the following interrupt from $886C and dispatch via the split target-minus-one table at $8860/$8866.
RTS at the end of the raster dispatcher. The two pushed bytes are the selected handler address minus one.
Select the panel character set and fixed scroll, and turn sprites off. Depending on patched operands, run periodic gameplay maintenance, the energy timer and sound work before acknowledging the IRQ.
Runtime immediate operand. The pause and round-setup routines set it to skip periodic work in the panel IRQ.
Patched immediate byte of LDA at $0418. Direct writes to this byte occur at $08C2, $0B8D, $0DDC.
High byte of the common IRQ exit target at the end of the panel handler.
Copy the position, colour and pattern shadows for sprites 4 to 7 from $C2-$CF to VIC-II and $C7FC-$C7FF. Merge the high sprite bits into the existing low sprite settings and enable all eight sprites.

Clear the ninth raster compare bit, acknowledge VIC raster status, wait until the beam leaves the slot's line and restore Y, X and A before RTI.
Return from NMI immediately. The regular IRQ path falls through here after restoring its saved registers.
Select title palette and raster settings, draw its text stream, poll for credits and start, then show the scores. After the idle timeout, use the attract-game path before returning to the title.
Patched immediate byte of LDX at $069D. Direct writes to this byte occur at $064E, $06A5, $06B9.
Set up video through $3E0C, change the title-area raster line to $4B and reset the display via $382A.

Select a round, replace several gameplay entry bytes with RTS and redirect the control call to $F306. Run the shared game loop with demo state, then restore original instructions and the normal control target before returning to the title.
Synchronize with the raster and read CIA1 matrix row 0 twice for a stable result. Debounce the sample and decode F1, F3 and F5 to add a BCD credit or start with one or two paid credits.
Immediate operand that retains the previous raw matrix sample for title input debounce.
Patched immediate byte of LDA at $07DA. Direct writes to this byte occur at $3FB6.
Low byte of the score-clear store operand, indexed by the active title player selection.
Split the packed BCD credit byte at $0296 into two nibbles, convert to the panel digit codes $10-$19 and put them at $C7C7/$C7C8.
Initialize the paired 20-byte arrays at $63 and $77 and seed selected slots before refreshing the fixed display.
Build the high-score display and poll start keys during its timeout while $084A updates the display on each pass.
Subtract two from the fine-scroll phase. On wrap shift the screen left and reset the sound-update flag. On an already-pending coarse step refresh the score column.
Copy nine split address pairs at $8832/$883B into the fixed positions of five-byte records beginning at $0883.
Nine absolute indexed loads receive their source addresses from $0863. At the index held in X they fill nonadjacent glyph slots beginning at $64 for an attract score row.
DEC decrements the indexed life count during the life-loss path. The initials comparison can patch the opcode to LDA absolute indexed, keeping the count intact.

Initialize a sprite entering from the screen edge when the round and motion flags allow it. Update its pattern, relative X and Y pursuit and determine hit or powered capture against Pac within its collision window.
The trailing ghost spawn path tests the sign of its direction before choosing sprite pattern and starting X coordinate.
Starting from pointer $033C, clear pages using indexed indirect stores, then continue through $FEC2.

Select the active player and round music. Each playing pass waits for raster line $A0, reads controls, checks pause and updates Pac, the objects and the terrain. Advance the round when the coordinate pair $9D/$9E matches the goal.
Wait for the game raster line, sample the controls, poll pause and update Pac, before moving the playfield or processing a life-loss flag.
Patched low operand byte of JSR at $0B9F. Direct writes to this byte occur at $06E0, $072E.
Patched high operand byte of JSR at $0B9F. Direct writes to this byte occur at $06E5, $0733.
Normally JMP to the life-loss path. The attract setup temporarily substitutes RTS so an end condition returns to its own caller.

Immediate replacing the default scroll step when the movement mode permits the override.
Execute the round-end routine before advancing $1D. The attract setup patches this first opcode to RTS.
Increment $1D and wrap $10 to 1. Increment the displayed round counter $1C in decimal mode, save per-player round state, and initialize the next round.
Start tune 0 and drive Pac's ready movement in the starting direction for a counter of $78 raster waits.
Ready-state movement loop. Wait on the raster, update Pac and advance scrolling until the countdown at $29 reaches zero.
Index paired player fields by $0250 and store round and trip information. Clear the two per-player fields at $8684 and $8686 and set the active player marker.

Try the other player first, falling back to the current player when the other has no lives. Restore scores and round, remove a displayed life marker and show the ready text. If neither has lives, discard the caller return address and take the title path.
Patched immediate byte of LDA at $0CFF. Direct writes to this byte occur at $3FB1.
Move the life-marker screen offset inward according to the active player, then restore the player's score and round fields.
Run the round-end sequence, check the round-specific extra-life cases, then use the round index modulo four to select a continuation through $8872 and $8876.
Reset gameplay flags, disable the three batches of multiplexed objects and clear the operands that override normal movement, raster work and scroll calculation.
Clear the three multiplex enable flags and restore the regular movement operands and per-round flags.
Advance the exit-scene sprite pattern at $0525, place the three companion sprites and play tune 8 during the timed scene.
Wait for the raster, update Pac and the scroll, then move the two extra horizontal positions left until $14 reaches zero.
Wait out one scene step and increment the X position. On carry the shared continuation returns, otherwise it publishes the new value.
For a fixed countdown, poll controls while forcing the requested horizontal direction right, update Pac, and advance the scrolling display.
Advance the scene animation, change horizontal speed on the ten-count divider and apply that speed to Pac's visible X positions.
Wait for the pose-update timing helper, read the controls and return to the exit-scene loop.
Patched immediate byte of LDA at $119B. Direct writes to this byte occur at $0E91, $1141.
Set up two low-numbered VIC sprites, initialize their X/Y and colours, and set their initial display flags.
Wait for raster line $C0, then fall through to the pattern toggle scheduled from the clock byte.
When the clock's low three bits are zero, toggle bit zero in both sprite pointers at $C7F8 and $C7F9.
Restore the interlude sprite data, clear expansion and set the shape, colour and coordinate shadows for the scene's two companion sprites.
Restore the map pointer workspace and sprite data. When Pac is airborne, select scene sprite art using the sign of the vertical phase and the current Y position.
Put Pac's two sprite layers in slots 0 and 1, initialize colours and sync all four low sprite X coordinates. The following sequence moves their positions and updates the display.
On the selected raster-clock phase, toggle the pattern fields for the scene sprites at $0525 and $0594.
Patchable immediate mask for the first scene sprite animation toggle. The entry image has $03 here.
Check the same animation phase and toggle the least significant bit of the pattern at $0594.
Wait for $10 raster checkpoints while running the single-pair animation.
Stage a $10-count timed step for the combined animation helper.
Wait for line $C0 and update both scene sprite pattern fields on the corresponding clock phase, repeating until X reaches zero.
Wait for $10 visits to raster line $C0 before returning.
Wait for line $A0 and toggle the least significant bit of Pac's sprite pattern when the low three clock bits are zero.
Split on the airborne flag $BC and jump control $33. Ground movement uses direction changes, the previous input and timers to manage speed, turning animation and the start of a jump.
On a nonzero directional request, compare with the previous request and facing. Raise the speed tier on an accepted renewed request and use timing before flipping the facing.
Start or restart the jump if the height and gameplay checks allow. Seed the vertical script from $889A, select the facing variant of the jump pose, set the airborne phase and request sound effect 1.
Patched immediate byte of LDA at $1556. Direct writes to this byte occur at $3715, $3722, $373E, $374B.
Allow a jump restart when $BD is set and $26 is clear. Update horizontal speed and facing while airborne, and select a pose using the current vertical phase.
Remember the requested direction, tick the vertical phase timer and advance both Pac sprite layers by the signed phase. Clamp the peak or land at the current terrain height.

Copy the eight-byte icon patch from $7FF5 to VIC character slot $1C.
Restore the saved side flag and write A as the sprite pointer, X as its colour and Y as its height. Take horizontal coordinate from $DD and put the carry-dependent X high bit in $D0.
Enter the sprite 4 shadow-write body with live carry, skipping the PLP entry immediately above.
Restore carry from the event setup, set sprite 3's X high bit accordingly and stage A, X, Y and $DD as its pattern, colour, Y and X.
Copy the sprite data from A, X, Y and $DD into the third raster band's sprite 2 patch operands. The saved carry selects the X high bit.
Update the third raster band's sprite 1 operands after restoring the event side flag.
Copy position, colour and pattern into sprite 3's patchable fields in the middle raster band.
Set middle-band sprite 3's fields using the current carry and $DD to encode its ninth X bit and low X position.

Set middle-band sprite 0's pattern, colour, Y and X fields. Select its X high bit with the event's carry.
Set top-band sprite 1 fields from A, X, Y and $DD using the live carry for the X high bit.
Use the sign of $2A and $ED displacement to move sprite 3 in the lowest band. Update the carried X high bit or release the object slot when it leaves the active span.
Normally jumps back to the scan. A paired-object retirement can patch this opcode to RTS while reusing the cleanup branch.
Apply directional displacement to the lowest sprite 2 X field, updating its high bit across byte wrap. Clear its staged display and active object when it leaves the visible area.
Move the lowest sprite 1 position. When it leaves the screen, restore the sprite's shared register flags before retiring the object.
Tail that stores the lower sprite 1 coordinate before returning to the active-object scan.
Retirement path for lower sprite 1. Mark it in the multicolour mask, clear its expansion and priority bits and zero its vertical coordinate.
Update the lowest sprite 0 X and its high bit, and hand a departing object to shared cleanup.
Jump operand at the end of the lower sprite 0 active-position path. Continues at $25EB.
Lower sprite 0 retirement stores. Restore its mode, expansion and priority bits and clear its Y before freeing the object slot.
Shift the second raster band's sprite 3 horizontally and retire the object as its ninth-bit and X limits require.
Shift the second raster band's sprite 2 horizontally and retire the object when its screen-span test fails.
Tail jump to the object scan. The paired-object path temporarily replaces JMP with RTS.
Middle-band sprite 1 cleanup body. The paired object code can write RTS here to return without changing its mode and position.
Tail that returns the updated position of middle sprite 0 to the scheduler.
Middle-band sprite 0 cleanup body. Change its mode and expansion bits, zero the staged Y and retire the active object.
Shift sprite 3's first-band position, maintaining bit 3 of the first band's high-X mask. Off-screen cleanup clears the staged Y coordinate.
Jump at the end of the top-band sprite 1 regular movement path.
First-band sprite 1 cleanup body. Clear its expansion bit, restore multicolour and finish retiring the object.
Jump at the end of the top-band sprite 0 regular movement path.
Patched high byte of the sprite-state load in the active collision path.
Walk the four tracked collision identifiers and remove the matching active object or linked sprite entries. In the empty case, set both event gates and consider a trailing ghost.

Part of the title renderer's credit text stream following the Quicksilva label.
End of the swapped title-side character set. The special terrain setup can copy a replacement glyph into this VIC slot.
VIC sprite patterns $40-$4F. The bank is $C000, so sprites fetch these Pac body and mouth animation frames from RAM under I/O.
VIC sprite patterns $50-$5F in RAM beneath the SID window. The large round Pac frames have a mouth opening on the opposite side to their counterparts at $D000.
VIC sprite patterns $60-$6F in RAM under colour I/O. This group contains standing, walking, airborne and small overlay art selected by the player motion routines.
VIC sprite patterns $70-$7F in RAM under the CIA and expansion I/O windows. Visible shapes include barriers and small enemy or item patterns.

VIC sprite patterns beginning at $80. The group contains small item, vehicle and object patterns. During the trip interlude the first eight pages of $E000 are also used to save the map pointer workspace.
Interior of the VIC sprite art bank. $E000-$E7FF can also hold the backed-up expanded map pointers between scene transitions.
VIC sprite patterns $90-$9F. The atlas shows drivers and vehicles in alternate facing and animation poses.
VIC sprite slot $97, in the portion reused by the trip scene.
Interior of VIC sprite slot $9F just before the $A0 group of vehicle frames.
VIC sprite patterns $A0-$A9, with wheel and body variants used by vehicle graphics.
Draw ten energy glyphs on the bottom row, reset the pill and related state and seed the timer bytes before a round.
When the power window is active, count it down and restore the selected round tune on expiry. Otherwise update the energy timer and bottom-row energy display.
When the warning gates allow it, XOR the ten bottom panel colour cells with the mask at $28 on the selected raster-clock phase.
Set $26, draw the ten-character message or marker from $C135 and give all ten cells colour 2.
Reset the tick delay using the remaining-energy index, then take the applicable round-end bonus branch or clear the panel if energy is exhausted.
As the round-end energy counter ticks, animate the energy icon and award a BCD score increment from the pip state table.
Enter the visible round setup path after the score display and interlude transitions.

Set the raster schedule and map buffer pointers for the selected round. Expand its maps, reset object and score support, draw the initial columns and establish Pac's starting sprite and movement state.
Initialize the scroll pointers and fill the screen from the current round's column dictionary and colour codes.
Patched low operand byte of LDA at $ED9D. Direct writes to this byte occur at $ED96.
Upper byte of the column pointer patched from the expanded high-byte map at initial playfield drawing.
Repeat the previous glyph into the column staging array with the current colour, then continue parsing.
Write the nineteen glyphs in $64-$76 and nineteen colours in $78-$8A down the screen column indexed by Y, beginning at $C4A0 and $D8A0. Return with Y incremented.
Draw the prepared glyph and colour arrays in a screen column at the current edge, using the buffer for the scrolling direction.

Use the round recipe to assemble column pointers and markers from the strip tables. Populate the event work area from per-round layouts and expand run-length encoded event-map values into $A5E0 onward.
Fetch the next strip ID via a patched address. Negative entries go straight to the high pointer list. Positive indices select the source streams and account for strip width.
Patched low operand byte of LDX at $EF75. Direct writes to this byte occur at $EF4B, $EF7A.
Patched high operand byte of LDX at $EF75. Direct writes to this byte occur at $EF51, $EF7F.
Patched low operand byte of LDA at $EFAD. Direct writes to this byte occur at $EF9F.
Patched high operand byte of LDA at $EFAD. Direct writes to this byte occur at $EFA5.
Patched low operand byte of LDA at $EFB4. Direct writes to this byte occur at $EF93.
High byte of the patched address used to read the current strip's low-pointer stream.
Record the last terrain boundary, clear the per-round object buffer and run the script that populates pairs with an encoded stride.
Expand count-and-value pairs into $A5E0 using the current round's pointer. Finish on count zero and process the saved round marker.
Advance the input pointer at $02/$03 and read its next byte, leaving Y equal to zero.
Patch the displayed trip digit, draw the ready and trip text, load interlude graphics and animate the four low sprites together, then restore the map work area.
Change the display, start tune 7 and show the game-over text. Wait for music to end, compare the score and present name entry when the score qualifies.

Read per-column terrain flags through $97 and height entries through $99. Update the floor operand and direction-dependent bounds, and put Pac into the airborne path when his Y differs from the new floor.
Patched operand selecting the alternate terrain-handling branch for the corresponding rounds.
Read a neighbouring terrain flag and map its set bit to a height. Return the default $DF if its marker does not select a height.
Read joystick port 2 from $DC00 first, then scan O, P and CTRL if no joystick direction or fire is active. Leave signed direction in $32, active-low jump in $33, and the jump debounce state in $34.
Drive all keyboard rows. If any input is detected, discard the immediate caller's return address to exit the attract pass.
Wait until the ninth raster bit is zero and the low raster byte equals $A0, then decrement $0F.
Zero $FF down to $02, leaving the port and its direction byte intact. The intended page-two loop stores zero at $0298, then exits because DEX from $88 leaves bit 7 set.
On an overlap, check the special tile-event state, clear the qualifying event and arm a four-step sprite change. Finish by removing the staged object or moving the normal sprite.
Patched immediate byte of LDA at $F37F. Direct writes to this byte occur at $F395, $F39E.
Patched immediate byte of LDA at $F3B5. Direct writes to this byte occur at $F3CB, $F3D4.

Patched immediate byte of LDA at $F4EE. Direct writes to this byte occur at $F504, $F50D.
